A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same EXOC study, with readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-C. Pages 2-13 are textually and visually identical; differences are confined to the first-page title and version/date stamp.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.3 report original predictive-performance and counterfactual-fairness experiments and ablations on synthetic and real-world datasets in Tables 1-3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental comparisons and ablation results in Tables 1-3 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: EXOC's auxiliary and control nodes, combined ELBO and custom loss, and inference procedure are unchanged. Appendix A's general framework and Appendix C's synthetic-data generation method are also identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic and real-world Law School regression and Adult income-classification tasks, with the same represented racial groups and counterfactual scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain exactly the same comparators: Constant, Full, Unaware, Fair-K, and CLAIRE. Their participation and descriptions are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain identical metrics, linear/logistic regression settings, sample counts, 80%/10%/10% splits, 8,000 training epochs, and gamma = 1.2.

E4.justification: Table 3's gamma sweep and Figure 3's comparison of using the control node versus predicted Y in the custom loss are identical. No ablations or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 reports five independent runs in both versions. The ± reporting in Tables 1-3 and shaded bands in Figure 3 are unchanged.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1-3 and Figure 3 are identical. For example, Table 2 reports EXOC Law School RMSE of 0.902 ± 0.005 and Adult accuracy of 0.748 ± 0.004 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, fairness bounds, causal-path arguments, loss formulations, and Appendix C's VAE objectives are unchanged, including Equations 1-26.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about improved counterfactual fairness, limited accuracy loss, and control over the fairness-accuracy balance.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of experimental results, and discussion of scalability, implementation complexity, and future optimization are identical.

D1.justification: Appendices B-C retain the same dataset details, hyperparameters, hardware/software descriptions, and generation instructions. Statements about supplementary code and the planned release of the Conda environment and Docker container are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to previous counterfactual-fairness approaches are identical.

P1.justification: The title corrects 'THOROUGH' to 'THROUGH', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Body prose, section organization, and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-3 retain identical formatting, captions, and placement. The title correction preserves the existing page layout.

improvement.justification: v2 removes a title typo and updates the version/date stamp. All scientific content, supporting evidence, and reproducibility information, including Appendices A-C, remain identical, so the editorial correction does not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
